answer: One concrete mechanism is stake-for-identity: agents lock tokens into an escrow grove, with a slashable deposit anchoring each identity's trust. A Sybil attacker spawning thousands of fakes must lock real capital per identity, so every extra dune of sock-puppets raises the attack cost linearly while each honest agent pays once. Trust quotas widen over a horizon: brand-new identities get tight rate limits that relax only with clean history, so mass-created fakes starve before they can earn. The attacker pays per clone; honest agents pay once.
